title: The Cuttlefish That Hypnotizes Prey With Its Own Skin 😱
script: It flashes hypnotic waves across its skin — and the crab just freezes. That's a cuttlefish hunting. It fires rippling pulses of light called 'passing clouds' directly at prey, overloading their nervous system. The crab locks up, cuttlefish strikes. It rewrites its own skin pattern 50 times per second — faster than any screen you own. Zero ink, zero noise, just light — and dinner is done. If you could flash any signal to freeze an enemy, what would it say? And that's why.
search_summary: Cuttlefish use hypnotic skin patterns called passing clouds to paralyze and stun prey before striking.
comment_question: Is this the most terrifying hunting trick in the ocean? 😳
source_note: Wood et al., Journal of Experimental Biology, 1994
